summary: The prompt systematically marks boundaries too early when a coordinate structure, prepositional phrase, or polarity-reversing element is incomplete. The three dominant failure modes are: (1) **head not yet arrived** (35% of premature verdicts) — emitting a noun or verb before its complement or modifier; (2) **wrong participant** (32%) — cutting before all parties in a relational phrase arrive; (3) **polarity not yet settled** (16%) — emitting affirmative or exclusive claims before negations or contrasts. The ranking audit shows the prompt over-trusts boundaries at relative position 0/3 (early in the sentence) and after commas, which are often safe but become dangerous when they fall inside incomplete coordinate structures or before polarity reversals. Rewrite [When to Segment] to forbid boundaries inside coordinate structures until all coordinates close, and inside prepositional phrases until the object arrives.
